bodyHTML:
Contributing guidelines

  • I have read CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Module(s)

mini.snippets

Question

This binding isn't taking effect, and I don’t know why:

require('mini.snippets').setup({
	mappings = {
	         jump_prev = "<c-r>",
	},
})

comment_data.body:
That is an interesting use case. I could reproduce, but partially: pressing `<C-r>` with the above setup did not jump within snippet but acted as default `:h i_CTRL-R` mapping (waited for a register key). It did work if cursor moved manually after snippet start or previous jump.

The culprit turned out to be an issue in Neovim (or rather Vim) itself. See vim/vim#20004. The reason for this is somewhat technical: 'mini.snippets' [calls `vim.fn.complete()` with no candidates](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/418ef4930ddabe80f449c6f1323f8b6abb172d1c/lua/mini/snippets.lua#L2776-L2779) whenever it moves cursor. This is meant as the best compromise to hide a possible completion menu (see [these details](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/418ef4930ddabe80f449c6f1323f8b6abb172d1c/lua/mini/snippets.lua#L2812-L2819)) which can be present even if `vim.fn.pumvisible()` says otherwise.

It turns out that specifically `<C-r>` mapping itself doesn't work in this situation and it does look like an issue in Vim/Neovim. Let's hope it will be resolved soon. In the meantime my suggestion is to not use `<C-r>` for jumping, I am afraid. It is also fairly useful for its built-in purpose: insert text from registers.
